text:
mike: FYI customer reported embeddings endpoint returning 512-d vectors but they expect 768. Also billing jumped dramatically this morning. Can we triage?

lina: who is the customer / route? any sample request IDs?

irene: Customer: AcmePayments (acct id: acct_8zYp). They attached a request id: req_20260315_7f3a9c. Reported via support ticket #5482. Said it started ~09:12 PST.

mike: route: /v1/embeddings with model "open-embed-xl" (expected 768). Sample curl from customer: 

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"open-embed-xl","input":"invoice text..."}'
```

support-bot: Received ticket reference and attached metadata to the thread. Please include request-level trace ids for faster lookup.

devon: quick hypothesis: we routed some requests to a compact variant (open-embed-sm, 512-d) during transient capacity pressure. There was a routing policy rollout yesterday that included a compatibility fallback mapping; maybe it matched incorrectly.

sre-alex: I'll pull traces for req_20260315_7f3a9c. Also share per-request latency breakdown from the observability logs: ingress/routing/queue/infer/postproc. If the fallback happened it should show a model_version header in the trace.

lina: mike can you share the API key last used (redacted) or have customer rotate? We need to confirm it's not mixing keys across accounts causing routing to a different tenant/model mapping.

irene: Customer rotated key after we asked. They also sent a repro script.

irene: repro python (from customer):

```python
import requests
headers = { 'Authorization': 'Bearer sk_live_xxx', 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }
data = { 'model': 'open-embed-xl', 'input': ['foo','bar'] }
resp = requests.post('https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings', json=data, headers=headers)
print(resp.status_code, resp.json())
```

mike: output they pasted: 
{"data":[{"embedding":[0.001, -0.02, ...(512 values total)...]}], "model": "open-embed-sm"}

lina: that confirms routing to the 512 model. Two prongs: why did routing pick that variant, and why did billing spike? The billing spike could be due to the customer sending duplicate requests (retries) when dimensions didn't match or due to different per-token/embedding pricing for the variant.

devon: there was a policy change: fallback_mapping now allows "open-embed-xl" -> [open-embed-xl, open-embed-sm] if capacity < 0.8. The weight was supposed to prefer xl, but a bug inverted the comparator in the rollout config for some regions. We should check the policy version serving in region us-west-2 at 09:12 PST.

sre-alex: pulled logs for req_20260315_7f3a9c: trace_id=7f3a9c-0001, routing_decision: open-embed-sm (fallback), routing_reason: capacity_threshold_breached, policy_version: 2026-03-14-v3b.

sre-alex: latency breakdown for that request (ms): ingress: 22, routing: 14, queue_wait: 310, gpu_infer: 48, postproc: 10, total: ~404ms. Batch size at the time: 64.

mike: queue_wait 310ms seems high. Could be batching/queue behavior after fallback. Customer complained about increased tail latency too.

lina: For observability asks from CS: they want per-request breakdown in Console and a trace link they can view. We currently have a trace link that requires org-level access; CS can't view it. Suggestion: add a short-lived shareable trace link in the Console UI and a dashboard tile: "Embeddings: per-request latency (p50/p95/p99) with model_version filter".

devon: also noticed we were charging the customer at open-embed-xl rate in billing records until 09:11:45 then switched to open-embed-sm rate after the fallback kicks in. Billing spike may be from retries + duplicate indexing jobs the customer ran. Need to reconcile invoice lines: charge id ch_9a12.

irene: I'll ask customer for logs of retries. They say a third-party ingestion job was rate-limiting and retried every 2s for ~20 minutes starting 09:10, sending identical requests.

mike: action items:
- devon: roll back the policy comparator fix to force prefer-xl or patch comparator today (ETA 1h).
- sre-alex: produce a shareable trace link and export the per-request breakdown for the ticket (ETA 30m).
- finance: reconcile charges for acct_8zYp and create a credit if duplicate retries caused extra billing (irene to loop in finance).
- devex: add a temporary dashboard tile and set alert for "embedding-dim-mismatch-rate" > 0.1% (low priority)

devon: I'm ready to patch. Patch will change comparator from "< 0.8" to "<= 0.8 and prefer_primary: true" and add unit test. Will deploy to canary in us-west-2 first.

sre-alex: shareable trace link for trace_id=7f3a9c-0001: https://console.redwood.example/trace/7f3a9c-0001?share=eyJhbGci... (expires in 72h)

irene: Customer confirmed they rotated keys and paused ingest. They asked if we can proactively detect when returned embedding dimension != requested model spec and auto-flag/notify.

mike: agree we should add a server-side validation check and return a structured warning header (X-Embedding-Dim-Mismatch) and a 200+warning payload (so not to break customers). Devex: add this to the spec.

devon: small note: some clients rely on implicit dimension check as signal; adding warnings is safer than switching status codes. We'll propose header + telemetry event "embedding.dim_mismatch" so Console can show rate.

lina: labeling: incident? it's a customer-impact config bug with billing consequence. I'll mark P2 and add to incident channel if we see wider scope.

irene: I'll coordinate credits once finance has numbers. Customer very appreciative of the fast response.

mike: thanks everyone. If any new traces come up, drop them here. :thumbsup:
